subject: Cross-region billing: allocation options & sample cost playbook
messages:
From: Sylvia Chen <sylvia@novacorp.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify billing for cross-region usage & discounts

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for the demo last week — team was impressed with the latency and the KV cache behavior for short-chat flows. We're narrowing vendors and I need a short, practical explanation of how Redwood would bill and apply discounts for our multi-region traffic. High level:

- Expected starting volume: ~1.2B tokens/month (grows to ~2B in Q4 if conversion targets hit)
- Regional mix: ~65% US, 25% EU, 10% APAC, with occasional APAC bursts from new accounts

Questions we need answered for procurement:
1) Do commit buckets and per-token discounts map to regions independently (a separate US commit, EU commit, etc.) or can we do a single global commitment and have usage routed across regions?
2) If we do a global (blended) commit, how do you handle price differentials (e.g., EU data residency + higher infra cost)? Any multipliers or reconciliation?
3) Are there additional cross-region charges (egress, inter-region transfer, data residency fees)?
4) What's the operational impact if we change region mix mid-quarter (spikes/bursts)?

Can you give us 1) two recommended packaging options (simple: per-region commits; and preferred: blended with adjustment), and 2) a sample cost table for our starting volumes? Procurement also asks for quick turn-around on an SOW or exhibit we can attach to an MSA.

Thanks — attaching our token forecast to make math easier.

— Sylvia
Sylvia Chen
Sr. Product Ops, NovaCorp
Attachment: product-usage-forecast.csv (csv)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Sylvia Chen <sylvia@novacorp.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify billing for cross-region usage & discounts

Hi Sylvia,

Appreciate the forecast — that makes this straightforward. Below is a concise comparison of the two approaches and a sample cost calc. I kept the math conservative; we can tighten numbers if you share a monthly token histogram.

Summary (short):
- Option A — Per-region commits: separate commit and discount schedule per region. Predictable per-region spend, but requires you to estimate traffic by region and can leave unused commits in one region during spikes elsewhere. Simpler procurement language.
- Option B — Blended/global commit with regional multipliers (recommended): single global commit pool for credits/discounts; region-specific multipliers adjust per-token charge to reflect cost differentials (e.g., EU +10%, APAC +15%). Good for teams with dynamic traffic and fewer contract amendments.

Sample pricing assumptions (illustrative):
- Base public-hosted rate (US): $0.00060 per token
- EU multiplier: +10% -> $0.00066 per token
- APAC multiplier: +15% -> $0.00069 per token

Discount tiers (applied to base price before multiplier):
- 0–100M tokens/month: 0% discount
- 100M–500M: 15% discount
- 500M–1.5B: 28% discount
- >1.5B: custom enterprise discount (typically 35–45% depending on commit length and billing cadence)

Example (1.2B tokens/mo, regional split as provided):
- Weighted base cost before discounts = 1.2B * $0.00060 = $720,000
- Discount band: most of this sits in 500M–1.5B -> 28% estimated blended discount -> $518,400 after discount
- Apply regional multipliers to allocate billed tokens: US (65%): $0.00060 * 0.72 = 0.000432 effective per token -> US cost ~ $336k; EU (25%): multiplier increases local price, APAC (10%) likewise. The platform will show a reconciliation table; for contracts we can supply the per-region reconciliation exhibit.

Operational notes:
- Blended pool with multipliers retains the simplicity of a single commit while honoring regional cost differences.
- Bursts across regions are covered up to burst rules in the contract; large, persistent shifts can be rebalanced at quarterly checkpoints with an amendment.
- Egress: generally there are no additional Redwood egress line items for API-hosted responses; if you request managed VPC or on-prem routing, there are separate network fees we'll call out.

Next steps I propose:
1) Marcus drafts a 1-page exhibit (Option A and Option B, with numbers) for procurement and legal.
2) If you prefer Option B, indicate whether you want a hard regional multiplier (fixed in contract) or a quarterly true-up.

If okay, I'll loop in our pricing lead and send a short exhibit and sample pricing worksheet by EOD tomorrow.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the ping. Suggested recommendation below — I built a concise playbook we can deliver to NovaCorp and procurement. I also attached a workbook with line-item math.

Recommendation (short): we offer both but lead with Option B (Blended global commit + fixed multipliers + quarterly true-up). Why: NovaCorp already has dynamic traffic and we can reduce contracting friction. Fixed multipliers make procurement comfortable that EU/APAC cost delta is explicit. Quarterly true-up keeps us protected from sustained region shifts.

Suggested multiplier (contractual):
- EU: +12%
- APAC: +18%
Rationale: we price slightly above the initial engineering cost delta to hedge network/regional infra variability and compliance/monitoring overhead. We can reduce multipliers for multi-year commitments.

Discount bands (finalized recommendation):
- 0–150M: 0%
- 150M–500M: 12%
- 500M–1.25B: 30%
- 1.25B+: 40% (requires 12–24 month commit term and annual true-up)

Burst and operational language (short bullets for exhibit):
- Short bursts: Allow +30% of monthly committed tokens for up to 2 non-consecutive days per month without penalty.
- Sustained overage: If monthly usage > committed + 30% for two consecutive months, apply true-up pricing for the overage at the higher of list or agreed blended price.
- Regional heavy-shift clause: If region mix shifts >25% from baseline for two consecutive quarters, parties will meet to rebalance multipliers or amend commit sizes.

Attachments: pricing-model-novacorp.xlsx (walks through cost table for 1.2B tokens with both Option A and Option B).

If you approve, I can convert these bullets into a 1-page contractual exhibit and a simple slide for Sylvia. Karthik — please check multipliers and confirm they align with capacity costs. Jordan — any objection from a sales-discount cadence perspective?

— Neha

- Recommended packaging: Option B — Blended global commit with contractual regional multipliers and quarterly true-up.
- Multipliers: EU +12%, APAC +18% (applied to base per-token rate).
- Discount bands: 0–150M (0%), 150M–500M (12%), 500M–1.25B (30%), 1.25B+ (40%, requires 12–24 month term).
- Burst policy: +30% for up to 2 non-consecutive days/month at no penalty; sustained overage triggers true-up.

Example estimate for your starting profile (1.2B tokens/month, 65/25/10 split):
- Estimated monthly invoice (rounded): $375,000–$540,000 depending on exact banding after quarterly true-up. The attached workbook shows line-by-line math and two scenarios (conservative and aggressive conversion).

Next steps if this matches your expectations:
1) Tell us whether you want the multipliers fixed in the contract or applied with a quarterly true-up (both are fine; fixed gives procurement certainty, quarterly true-up gives flexibility).
2) If fixed, we will generate an exhibit and an initial SOW; if true-up, we will include the reconciliation cadence in the exhibit.
3) I will create a DocuSign for the exhibit once legal signs off — planning to share the DocuSign link in 24–36 hours.
